title: Wytham Woods (England) — deciduous forest, every tree as ground truth (Q-ForestLab)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ) from the Q-ForestLab instance segmentation benchmark (Ghent University). Test area of the Wytham Woods plot (temperate deciduous forest, Oxfordshire, England). Every point carries the manually assigned tree ID (122 reference trees ≥ 10 cm DBH). Canopy height (H95) 19 m, PAI proxy 3.6, cover 87 %; 12.1 % of the light reaches the ground vertically (estimate from the point cloud, no occlusion correction). Source: Zenodo 16875688, CC BY 4.0.

source.dataset: TLS forest instance segmentation benchmark: 2983 manually segmented trees from four plots (Cherlet et al. 2026, Q-ForestLab). Testgebiet des Plots Wytham Woods (gemaessigter Laubwald, Oxfordshire, England).

legend.title: Colourings

items.label: Height above ground — the dataset has no camera colour
Ground truth — one colour per tree, segmented by hand
Light at the ground (daily mean, equinox): dark blue 0.1 % … yellow 100 %

legend.note: Strata relative to canopy height; light = estimate from the point cloud without occlusion correction.

annahmen.licht: Transmission = product (1 − cover) of the traversed voxels; cover = 2 cm points / (v/0.02)²
annahmen.grenze: no scanner positions, no occlusion correction; upper canopy underestimated → gaps rather overestimated; result depends on voxel size; interpret values relatively
